value.rationale: The squared variance of a 1-Lipschitz observable is a natural metric-measure concentration/average-distortion invariant. This theorem solves it over a continuous natural Euclidean rectangle family, compares real and Hilbert target dimensions exactly, identifies all equality maps, and determines the unique worst shape for the relative gap. The strict scalar–Hilbert defect shows a genuine target-geometry obstruction; this structural classification is not a renamed standard estimate or arbitrary finite table.
